reasoning: search: heap/branch-bound - CPython-law tuple heap (scalar, NaN-first ordering), random-access label gather/scatter, and short adjacency rows (avg degree 4 in the row0-scale probe; characterized graphs similar): phase-one eligibility is elementwise IEEE-composable (fast_lt/fast_le reproduce exactly under SIMD NaN semantics) but width-4/8 within degree-2..8 rows wastes lanes, and the loop is memory-latency-bound, not arithmetic-throughput-bound
adjust: a d_count-length min scan per origin - vectorizable but negligible in every profiled split (CPU_LAYOUT attributed adjust ~3% of kernel)

fold: the ONLY wide-vector region (elementwise exp / ordered sums over d_count, where the engine's fastmath vectorization lives) is contractually ON THE CANONICAL PLANS, not in the native surface - numba already emits its own SIMD inside the pinned legacy plan, and a native SIMD fold would create a third arithmetic mode forbidden by the SPEC fold-profile split
label-init fill is memset-class; the ISA report confirms the binary is generic x86-64-v1 while the host is v4-capable, i.e. any variant claim would have to come with its own per-regime attribution
